core.title: Give each acceptance field its own generator prompt sourcing that field's rule
core.given: You are composing or maintaining the generator prompts that author acceptance fields
core.when: you write or change the prompt for any acceptance field (id, urn, harness, route, given, when, then)
core.then: Give each field its own prompt, and have that prompt source its field's section of the acceptance convention and state that section's rule as a requirement.
prefer: The id prompt requires the acceptance convention's id rule: the acceptance id matching the stack's acceptance identifier pattern (profile: urn.acceptance_id).

The urn prompt requires the acceptance convention's urn rule: derive the acceptance urn with the stack's acceptance-urn construction idiom from its defined inputs (profile: idiom.acceptance_urn_derivation).
The harness prompt requires the harness that best exercises the outcome, from the harness kinds the stack's acceptance convention offers.
The route prompt requires the acceptance convention's route rule: populate the route's layers and sequence so actions flow through the stack's layers in dependency order.
The given prompt requires only the preconditions the action needs before it runs (e.g. authentication, test data builders, time, stubbing, configuration).
The when prompt requires the trigger in the shape of the chosen harness.
The then prompt requires assertions that prove the outcome.
avoid: One generic prompt that writes all fields at once.

A field prompt that does not source its section, or that softens its rule (e.g. hand-built urns, harness picked by habit, unneeded preconditions, generic triggers, assertions not tied to the outcome).
core.why: Each acceptance field has its own authoring rule in the acceptance convention, so each field's prompt sources that section.
evidence: The generator configuration has one prompt per acceptance field (id, urn, harness, route, given, when, then), and each prompt sources the matching section of the acceptance convention.
Each field prompt states its field rule (listed in prefer) as a requirement.
The generated acceptance id matches the stack's acceptance identifier pattern (profile: urn.acceptance_id).
The generated urn equals the urn derived by the stack's acceptance-urn construction idiom with its input mapping (profile: idiom.acceptance_urn_derivation).
The generated route's layers and sequence are both populated and ordered by the stack's layer order (profile: roles.layers).
The generated when uses the chosen harness's shape, and the generated then contains assertions on the outcome.
verification: Term: the generator prompt is the LLM authoring prompt for one acceptance field.
Scope: the rule governs the prompts only. It does not require that acceptances be produced by generators, and acceptance artifacts edited by hand are out of scope.
The id check recognizes the acceptance identifier pattern from the profile (urn.acceptance_id); no identifier components or padding are hardcoded in the rule.
The harness vocabulary is open: the check accepts the harness values the stack's acceptance convention offers, not a fixed list.
The route check recognizes the layer order from the profile (roles.layers), not a list hardcoded in the rule.

Whether a prompt's wording carries its field's rule is judged (llm_judged), not mechanically parsed; telling which field prompts changed needs a structural diff observer over the generator configuration (needs_new_observer).

values: acceptance-field generator prompt added or modified (id, urn, harness, route, given, when, then)
generator prompts not split per field
a field prompt does not source its convention section or omits/weakens its field rule

fires: Planner writes the generator prompts/configuration that author acceptance fields (id, urn, harness, route, given, when, then).
Planner revises an existing acceptance-field generator prompt, e.g. the harness or route prompt.
Planner consolidates or splits acceptance-generation prompts.
doesNotFire: Planner creates or edits an acceptance by hand without using or changing any generator prompt. This rule does not require that acceptances be generated.
Coder implementing tests or production code for an acceptance that is already authored.
Editing prose or docs that only reference acceptance ids or fields and contain no acceptance-field generator prompt.
A task that merely mentions harness, route, urn or acceptance without concerning the acceptance-field generator prompts.

profileRequirements.meaning: The layer order, in dependency order, that the route prompt must require the acceptance route to flow through, and that the route check recognizes.
The identifier pattern an acceptance id must match, whatever components and padding the stack's format uses, which the id prompt must state as a requirement and the id check recognizes.
profileRequirements.bunValue: AC-{STEP}-{NNN}, where STEP is the step code and NNN is the zero-padded index

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's construct that derives an acceptance URN from its inputs, with the exact input mapping, which the urn prompt must state as a requirement.
profileRequirements.bunValue: URNBuilder.acceptance(wagon slug, WMBT ID, harness code, sequence)

proposedKeys.meaning: The identifier pattern of one acceptance (not itself a URN) that every acceptance id in this stack must match, in whatever components and padding the stack's format uses.
proposedKeys.bunValue: AC-{STEP}-{NNN}, where STEP is the step code and NNN is the zero-padded index
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: urn.acceptance describes only the acceptance URN's overall shape (acc:<domain>:<acceptance-id>) and no other key describes the non-URN identifier pattern an acceptance id itself must match; no other group covers artifact identifier formats.

proposedKeys.meaning: The stack's construct that derives an acceptance URN from its inputs, with the exact input mapping.
proposedKeys.bunValue: URNBuilder.acceptance(wagon slug, WMBT ID, harness code, sequence)
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: urn.acceptance gives the URN's shape and tooling.urn_resolver resolves a URN to its artifact; no existing key describes the construction idiom or its derivation inputs.

bunOnly.text: harness prompt requires the harness that best exercises the outcome (unit/http/event/ws/e2e/...).
bunOnly.reason: The concrete open harness list is content of the stack's acceptance convention (owned by the harness-selection rule); the core refers to the harness kinds the stack's acceptance convention offers and imposes no fixed list.

bunOnly.text: Harness values include unit, http, event, ws and e2e. The list is open.
bunOnly.reason: The concrete harness vocabulary is acceptance-convention data, not a parameter this rule's check consumes; the core verification keeps only the open-list fact.

neutralityNotes: The convention itself is stack-neutral: it governs LLM authoring prompts for acceptance fields, and given/when/then/why, activation and scope were already free of stack names. The concrete field-rule contents the prompts must state are profile-bound where the core's duties are parameterized: the acceptance identifier format is bound by the proposed key urn.acceptance_id (Bun value: AC-{STEP}-{NNN}, step code plus zero-padded index), so the core requires only that the id prompt and the generated id follow the profile's pattern without naming any identifier components or padding; the acceptance-urn construction idiom and input mapping (URNBuilder.acceptance(wagon slug, WMBT ID, harness code, sequence)) is bound by the proposed key idiom.acceptance_urn_derivation; the route layer order is bound by roles.layers. Both new keys are pending owner approval and are also listed in profileRequirements so the Bun values stay bound. The open harness list (unit/http/event/ws/e2e/...) remains realization data (bunOnly) because it is content of the stack's acceptance convention and the core's check imposes no fixed or parameterized list on it, only that the harness best exercises the outcome. The acceptance-field names (id, urn, harness, route, given, when, then) are treated as the acceptance artifact's schema, not stack names, and stay in the core. Illustrative example lists (http request, unit target, event topic; status, body, headers, error, metrics) are not repeated in the core; bun.json remains the worked reference example.
